Hi Marta / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and the two asks I promised:

Summary from our call
- Primary goal: move the in-product search reranking from CPU-based service to an LLM reranker for richer results and higher conversion.
- Target latency: p95 <= 120ms for 512-token calls (single-turn rerank).
- Current constraints: runs in us-east, procurement looking at Q1 budget, legal needs SOC2 evidence.

What I attached
- atlas_latency_readout_v1.pdf: quick synthetic readout we ran against a 3B reranker on A100s (short-form tests using sequence len 512 / 5-shot prompts).
- kernel-profiles.csv: micro-benchmarks for attention kernels and KV cache memory for their expected sequence lengths.

Immediate asks (A/B):
1) Technical confirm: can you confirm the p95 SLO target is still the right priority vs. throughput? If throughput (tokens/sec) matters more we reframe the plan.
2) Timing: is procurement still Q1, or has that slid? If Q1, we should lock a dedicated capacity window to guarantee p95 targets.

If useful I can loop in Evelyn (solutions) for an in-depth bench plan and a live test slot next week.

Next steps I propose
- You review the attached latency readout.
- Reply with prioritization (latency vs throughput) and procurement window.
- If you want a live bench: pick 2x 1-hour windows and Karthik will scope the test configuration.

Thanks — will follow up if I don't hear back by next Tuesday.

Best,
Logan Wright

Subject: Re: Post-discovery follow-up — latency readout and timing for next steps

Hi Marta / Tom —

Following up on a couple of the technical items we discussed. I ran a few clarifying micro-benchmarks after the call and added the kernel-profiles.csv so you can see the expected KV memory growth and per-step kernel times. High-level notes:

- Test hardware: single A100-80GB, batch size 8, sequence lengths 128 / 512 / 1024.
- Observed p50 / p95 / p99 for 512 tokens (warm cache): 28ms / 98ms / 220ms.
- Throughput: ~1,800 tokens/sec at batch size 8 for steady-state generation; with batching disabled (latency-first) we hit ~260 requests/sec for single-turn 512-token rerank calls.
- Memory/kv: KV cache increases ~1.6GB per 512 tokens; kernel times dominated by flash-attn at longer sequences.

Assumptions: short context (single-turn rerank), model quantized to int8 stripe; these numbers are optimistic for the 3B model we used. For your production model (4–7B family) expect ~1.2–1.8x the times above unless you opt for tuned kernels.

If you'd like, we can:
- Run the identical workload on a dedicated node in our lab and share the raw traces (latency histograms + perf logs).
- Supply a compact SLO doc for procurement showing p95 claim, error budget, and fallbacks.

- Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: kernel-profiles.csv (csv)
